method: WebSearch to identify candidate MoUs/events, then WebFetch on the actual press release, wire story, or business-press article to verify company name, HQ, sector, figure and any follow-up status before recording. Primary sources used: Invest UP / invest.up.gov.in press releases (several blocked by TLS/403 on direct fetch, so relied on wire coverage that quoted them), Business Standard, ThePrint, Khaleej Times, Zawya, Gulf News, Swarajya, FreePressJournal, BusinessWorld, IndiaBriefing, TelecomTalk, IndianMasterminds, BusinessToday, ANI (mostly blocked, used syndicated republishes instead), and corporate-registry listings (ClearTax/Panjiva) used only to confirm a signatory company actually exists as a going concern in India. This session's WebSearch quota (200 calls) was exhausted partway through; a handful of promising leads (Star Consortium Pvt Ltd, Fuji Silvertech/Fujisilvertech, BAE Systems, individual UK/Singapore signatories beyond SLG Capital, the Jan 2026 WEF Davos UP delegation, and a separately-reported 'Rs 90,000 crore with various Japanese companies' headline) could not be individually verified and are listed as open leads in negative_notes rather than included as verified MoUs.

negative_notes: Minda Corporation (Spark Minda / Uno Minda group) appears prominently in both the Feb-2026 Japan-visit coverage and the Aug-2026 UP-Japan Investment Meet (Rs 1,166 crore, YEIDA Sectors 10 & 24) but is headquartered in India (New Delhi/Noida) and was excluded per this sweep's foreign-only scope, despite being marketed alongside genuinely Japanese signatories.

Fuji Silvertech / Fujisilvertech Concrete Pvt Ltd was named in one secondary source (an X/Twitter post attributed to 'The Uttar Pradesh Index') as part of the Feb-2026 Japan-visit MoU batch, but could not be corroborated in any article this sweep fetched, and its sector/HQ could not be independently verified. Left out rather than guessed.

BAE Systems (UK) was reported as having met UP delegation officials ('preparing for big investment') around UPGIS-2023, but no source found describes an actual signed MoU — this looks like an exploratory meeting, not a verified MoU, so it was excluded.

UK partner-country session at UPGIS-2023 reportedly produced '6 MoUs in security, technology and defence sectors,' and the UK announced defence/aerospace/medical investment intent generally, but no individually-named UK company signatory could be found in accessible coverage.

Singapore's partner-country session reportedly produced 6 new MoUs (urban infrastructure, waste management, IT parks, data centres, education) plus a separate ~Rs 29,000 crore 'spiritual and eco-tourism' investment pledge from unnamed 'investors from Singapore.' Only SLG Capital could be individually verified; the rest are unnamed in the press coverage this sweep found.

Star Consortium Private Limited was named alongside SLG Capital as signing a ~Rs 2,000 crore data-centre/logistics MoU with UPSIDA, but this sweep could not confirm whether it is foreign- or India-headquartered, so it was left out rather than assumed foreign.

Denmark-UP 'Smart Laboratory on Clean Rivers' (SLCR), signed as a ~Rs 1,000 crore MoU at UPGIS-2023 and formally launched in 2024 by NMCG/IIT-BHU/Government of Denmark, is a genuine, well-documented, and (unusually for this dataset) confirmed-active bilateral partnership — but it is a government-to-government MoU, not an individually-named foreign company, so it was excluded from the mous array per this state's task scope.

A May-2023 MoU between the UP government and Gyeongsangbuk-do province (South Korea) was found (invest.up.gov.in press release), but this is again a sub-national government partner, not a company, and was excluded on the same basis.

This sweep's central hypothesis going in — that UP's Ground Breaking Ceremony 3.0/4.0 events would give unusually good, checkable individual-company conversion data for UPGIS-2023 MoUs — did NOT pan out from publicly accessible coverage. GBC coverage found (organiser.org, thestatesman, businesstoday-style recaps) reports only aggregate figures (e.g., '1,406 projects worth Rs 80,000 crore' for GBC 3.0; '14,000 projects worth ~Rs 10 lakh crore' for GBC 4.0) and, where individual companies are named at all, they are overwhelmingly domestic real-estate/industrial names (Godrej Properties, Mahagun Infratech, Theme County, Roseberry Estate) rather than the internationally-branded UPGIS-2023 MoU signatories tracked in this file. No source found cross-references a specific foreign UPGIS-2023 signatory (e.g. IKEA, Lulu Group, HMI Group, SLG Capital) against a specific GBC groundbreaking event, so none of the 'no follow-up news found' verdicts above should be read as 'confirmed stalled' — they reflect a genuine absence of public foreign-company-level conversion tracking, not a documented failure to convert.

A January-2026 WEF Davos delegation reportedly secured UP investment-proposal MoUs worth 'nearly Rs 3 lakh crore,' and a separately-headlined figure of 'Rs 90,000 crore with various Japanese companies' also surfaced in search results — neither was chased down to individually-named foreign companies in this sweep due to running out of WebSearch budget partway through; both are flagged here as open leads for a follow-up sweep.

The exact calendar date of Ground Breaking Ceremony @3.0 could not be pinned down independently in this sweep (multiple candidate source pages returned HTTP 403); it is placed provisionally in the Aug/mid-2023 window based on its being reported as the ceremony preceding GBC @4.0 (Feb 2024).
